description:
Korean Effigy Dolls. ⁣
⁣
Effigy are representation of a person and is present in many traditions. In Korea, spirit tablets in ancestral shrines, or other shrines for housegods and deities are also a form of effigy. ⁣
⁣
These are effigy dolls, their main purpose are for rituals called 대수대명 (Daesu-dae-myung). We collect all the negativity that a specific person is affected by and put it into the doll, performing the ritual providing aid and relief. ⁣
⁣
There are many types of effigy used in the rituals of a Korean shaman -the mudang. Traditional effigy used in the rituals is dried pollack fish. Depending on the severity of affected person, hair and nail clippings are used to dress the effigy, or undergarments of the person. ⁣
⁣
When a person is in their samje cycle of the 3 calamities, many request the 대수대명 ritual to help with the cycles of bad luck. Or when someone is sick, needing a cleansing or an exorcism, this powerful ritual is performed. ⁣
⁣
⁣
We have a very special kut ceremony today - and again, no sleep before a kut ceremony. ⁣
⁣
Todays kut is for an elderly korean halmoni (grandmother). Her story is an incredible journey of sheer willpower, and the hearts devotion she given to her practice. Its also made me realize that I need to go deeper into my practice, I owe it to myself and my spirits and most importantly for my clients. ⁣

description:
Eopsin, god of stored wealth (household fortune). ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
2 winters ago, in the front of my home I spotted a snake blocking my path.  A few months later, another snake appeared. It was such an odd occurence to have a snake in front of home not only once but twice - in NYC, in winter. ⁣⁣
I notified my spiritmom, she instructed me to move out of the house asap. I was upset, and did not listen. I wanted to stay for a few years. Little did I know, the signifance and the meaning of those events for me. ⁣⁣
Eopsin 업신 is a gasin 가신, a house deity that protects the home and the family's financial possessions. The sacred ways in which eopsin is emobodied varied, and included danji (earthen pot), straw bundles, animals like snake, weasel, toad, mice, etc. The most common is a black serpent, or a snake. ⁣⁣
⁣
When a sepent is seen leaving the permieters of a home, its a fortelling sign of family's decline, money loss, and  winds of unfavorable events. Some viewed the snake as ancestral spirits leaving, that you've lost their favor and protection. 조상이 더는다. Either way, snakes leaving your home is an inauspicious sign. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Things got much noisier within my family, alot more headaches and lost money. We experienced so much bad luck, even scammed by our landlord and by my client. We did move out of that home, and now in a better home.⁣
⁣
▪︎NOTE: this does NOT apply to everyone. I'm being flooded with messages about the shamanic meaning of snakes. ⁣I have altars and offerings set monthly to my house gods and deities. This would make perfect sense for my situation, and what I do. It would be difficult to apply it to others. ⁣⁣

description:
In the kut ceremony various offerings are made to the many gods. Meat offering would either consist of either a pig or a cow. ⁣
⁣
Cows are very sacred to our ancestors, some treated their cows better than their own children.  Cows were sacred because of the help, often cows help plow the fields and used as a workhorse. In older times there were gods and goddess for the cow pen & stable and for the birth of cows. Cows are valuable to Koreans. ⁣
⁣
I read somewhere that pigs were used as offerings more so than the cow because cows were too precious to give up. Also pigs are seen as wealthy and lucky animals. ⁣
⁣
I wonder if that can be one of the reasons why pigs are use for Daegam, the greedy god who oversees wealth, luck and prosperity. ⁣
⁣
Also the type of animal offering is an indicator of the kut ceremony magnitude. If its a huge kut, with clients spending lots of money for the ceremony then a cow is used. If its an average ordinary kut, a pig head or a whole pig is used - especially if it involves asking for more luck and blessings. ⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣

description:
Have a blessed Dong-ji - Winter Solstice. ⁣
⁣
Today was an incredibly hectic day. Cleaning the house in preparation for my mom, staying for the week. Tomorrow we have a kut 굿 ceremony/ritual that took two days of prep work. ⁣
⁣
Today is also Dong-ji (Winter Solstice), I wiped down my altar, cleaned all my offering bowls, cooked red bean porridge as sacrificial offering, laid out all the offerings around our home....with 2 kids at home sick. ⁣
⁣
I unfortunately did not have designated bowls for my shrine, to use as an offering plate. Altar offering bowls, plates and servingware are separate from the bowls/plates of personal use. So I improvised, used clear cups as offering bowls for the red bean porridge. ⁣
⁣
This reminded me that not every offering spread is grand or perfect, especially during older times when food were seasonal. How did mudangs hold ceremonies, ritual rites and other services when supplies werent readily available -they improvised.⁣
In the winters, no fruit grew or was available to use as offering. Instead they made sweet cookies made with honey, dried fruits and nuts using the honey cakes as an alternative. ⁣

description:
When we offer liquor to our ancestors, each cup must be poured one at a time, since there is a mini-ritual involved. 
We pour one cup, and above the incense smoke we twirl the liquor THREE times clockwise and then THREE times counterclockwise. Then the liquor is placed on the ancestors altar. 
This is done for each of the ancestors liquor cups. For shamanic kut 굿 ceremony, we have 6 liquor offerings for the ancestors. When all offerings are placed on the altar, you must bow 3 times. 
This is done during ancestral rites known as jesa 제사 also in shamanic ceremony/ritual. Whenever liquor is offered to the ancestors, this does not apply for offerings to the gods.

description:
Today is Buddhas birthday known as the "Day Buddha Arrived " in Korea. This morning we set the altar with all the offerings. On this day, traditionally we eat a vegetarian bibimbap with barley rice. 
Spirit mom drummed, sanged and banged her mokugyo performing ceremonial rites for Buddhas birthday. 
Early afternoon we finished the ceremony,  my sisters and I cleared everything away. Since we were all just chatting away, spirit mom took out the delicate colored papers so we can fold, while we chatted. 
These paper flowers are offerings we make at every kut ritual, these flowers will be put on the altar meant for the ancestors during the kut ceremony. 
The flower serves a roles as a tangible offering to show the spirits dedication and devotion. The origins of the paper flower started when flowers were incredibly hard to come by during cold wintery months.
These paper flower also play a huge role within the Korean Buddhist as well, used for many rites and ceremonies. 
We have several kut ceremony/ritual happening back to back, grateful for the opportunity to learn and grow as a mudang.

description:
Yakgwa (약과) is up on my altar from this past new moon offerings. ⁣
⁣
It's a traditional Korean cookie, usually with a flower shape being pressed into wooden molds and some times decorated with nuts and/or dates. Yakgwa literal translation is "medicinal confection", as 'yak' means medicine and 'gwa' means cookie or fruit. The medicinal part refers to the large amounts of honey used in it. ⁣
⁣
They were mainly used as offerings for ancestral rites, court banquets, holidays and special celebrations. ⁣
⁣
This snack has one of the longest history  within the Korean cuisine, ⁣originating during the Three Kingdoms era. People would use powered grains mixed with other ingredients, to shape them into fruit or flower shapes when they couldnt find any actually fruits to use during ancestral rites, court banquets, ceremonies and rituals. ⁣
Due to their usage for rituals, its gained popularity and became the must-have food for those occasions. So popular that they had shortages of its main ingredient such as flour, honey, etc.⁣
⁣
Ancient kings of Goryeo even banned people from making of the yakgwa. ⁣
In modern Joseon era, these snacks were mostly enjoyed by the upper Yangban social class. Wheat, honey, and other scarce precious ingredients were highly regarded. ⁣
⁣

description:
(1/2) 법사⁣ - The sutra readers of a ritual or ceremony. ⁣⁣
⁣
Often males, and possess multi talents in singing, music and crafts. Their work is focused on aiding the mudangs. In a ceremony or ritual,  the main focus is on the mudang as the ritual center.  The nucleus of the cell, meaning no mudang - no ritual or kut. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
During a ritual or ceremony, 법사 will provide musical support while the mudangs jumps, dances, receiving the gods and spirits directly through trance spirit-possession. ⁣⁣
법사 training are also very intensive, mandatory to memorize the hundreds of different sutras used for space clearing, blessings, exorcism, prayers, chants while having musical gift with the different drums used in a ritual or ceremony. They are also gifted crafters, making paper talismans with sutras, gods and protective deities cut out from sacred paper. While many will dismiss what seems like mere paper craft decorations - unknowingly aware of the magic, energy and presence it commands. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
There many types of beob-sa, some will have strong gods energy 신끼 (shin-ki), afflicted by the spirits sickness, the divine sickness of 신병 (shinbyeong) eventually receive confirmation from other mudangs who says they are "the gods product". Those sutra readers 법사 will most likely receive their 신내림 (gods descent ritual- initiaition). ⁣⁣

Chuseok has a meaning of 'Autumn evening with a bright moon'. Its a holiday for ancestral memorial services and the tending to ancestral graves. Day starts with preparing an offering table with steamed rice and seasonal foods. Offerings must include (토란국) toran-guk, taro soup. (송편) songpyeon called pine needle rice cakes shaped half moon rice cakes with filling.⁣

Its also a holiday that signals to the farmers that it was time to relax and enjoy fruits of their labor.  Korean farmers tried to predict harvest based in the moon's shape, color hue through moon divination called (달점) dal jeom. Red moon sinaled signs of drought and white foretold lots of rain, interpretation varied from region and farmers. ⁣
⁣
I will be setting my altar tomorrow with all the traditional offerings. Happy Chuseok⁣ 💖🙏📿⁣

description:
Absolutely adore and love Korean pine trees. 💕 Each curve and twist of the tree I feel inspiration and honor. When I see a beautiful pine tree, I think of ancestors. Like a great big grandfather or grandmother tree, wise with honor and integrity, and always there. 🙇‍♀️⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
Long ago, there was a giant pine tree and the King with his caravan was travelling until the tree block their path. The King demanded the tree bends to let them pass or else he will come back to tear it down. Just then the branches twisted, turned and parted to allow the King to pass. The tree instead was commemorated as the King's tree. I heard its based a real tree and has been protected as sacred. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
Pine trees is Korea's national tree, its presence is incredibly symbolic.  Pine is also used when a family welcomes a new baby, or its adorned on a casket when someone passes. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
There's even an old Korean village that fitted their home around the tree with their trunks and branches. Imagine having a Korean pine tree just growing out of your livingroom.  I been looking for years if Korean pine trees are legal to plant, because I soon as I can get land - would really like to plant the tree. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
⁣Pine trees are sacred, often used for their cleasing abilities and for their longevity and vitality.  Pine trees also can represent the house gasin spirit Songju (the roof beam god). Along with births and funerals, pine trees are adorned in vases at weddings as the sharp needles keeps evil and negativity out, blessing the space as a protector of humanity, representing the resilient spirit of the people. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
I love Korean pine trees. ⁣❤⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣

Trees were sacred, and were seen as god pillars in Korea.  Mongolians view the trees as 'sacred gateway'. Its said, Koreas connection to the Baikal region Buryats part of the Altaic language is where our Koreas tongue -dialect is rooted from. ⁣⁣

Mudang have rigid and strict structures, the daily task of temple/shrine upkeeping. We play a concert maestro, making sure our gods are happy, and synced in harmony. When we work, moving as one fluid spiritual being, a cohesive relationship.

description:
Great 🌕 Full Moon Festival  Dae-Boreum 대보름. Also a day of folk magic and rituals. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
This auspicious day is spent strengthening bonds and ties with your neighbors and the community.  Its a time when the community and villagers unify to participate, working with one another for the peace and well-being of the village or community. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣ A Earth ritual of Jisin-bapgi 지신밟기 means to 'Step on Earth' which a folk ritual dedicated to the land, Earth goddess or land spirit called Jisin 지신. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Purpose of this ritual is to being prosperity,  chasing away negativity and expelling evil with the loud percussion of the drums and gongs. While they sing and chant good wishes. The  band would also visit the surrounding homes spreading cheer, blessings and chasing away negativity. Homeowners would come out to greet the band with food, drinks and money. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
A moon house (spirit house or pillar) called Dal-jip 달집 is built by the community. Children and adults would write their wishes and tie it to the branches of the moon house. As the full moon rises, the moon house is set on fire,  a sacred fire meant to bring in blessings. The louder the fire crackles means the greater the "exorcism" as it cleanse and purifies. Like how firecrackers are used to chase evil, expelling negative forces. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣
I hope to one day to have a space for rituals, prayers and moon houses. ❤ community. ⁣⁣

description:
[Post 2/2] Trigger Warning ⁣
Domestic Violence ⁣
⁣
Then later, I walked out and left my other relationship after many years. There was dishonesty, but also the feeling of low-self worth. He wasnt physically abusive with his hands, but his words stung like blades. Constant verbal assault, making me feel inferior and insignificant to the world. He would sit down, and ask me what is it I do, that's so good and pick apart everything about me. If he was late to a meeting because he overslept, he would kick me out of the house early morning. ⁣
⁣
I realize despite my vow to myself of not repeating my parents abusive cycle.  I was here creating my own, making excuses and accepting this life. ⁣
⁣
Abuse was the only thing constant in my life. Abused by my own family...my cousin "Gloria" would give use corporal punishment like holding a heavy wooden chair over my head for hours. At night she would send my cousin Peter and siblings into the room, while she held a knife to my throat. Or hit our backs with a metal mop pole because we failed to hold wooden chairs over our head for hours. ⁣
⁣
I've had many incidents of sexual assault by my trusted friends, and others including my brothers Tae Kwon Do teacher. ⁣
Despite abuse being a constant factor in my life, I rised above my situation. I finally put my foot down because I refuse to be held down. I learned to find my voice, strength and courage to finally stand up for ME. ⁣
As a mother of 2 young boys, I teach them humility, respect and compassion. ⁣
At times, the trauma of my abuse can hinder me especially towards my husband. When I forget he is on my side, supporting all the many parts of me. ⁣
⁣If you are in an abusive relationship or setting, it's not your fault. We dont control the actions of others, but are in control of our thoughts, feelings and action. ⁣
One good friend taught me, "Living well is the best revenge" and I intend fully to live well in my mission, and path or kiss my mudang ass.
⁣

description:
The 5 colors of Korean shamanism,  similar to Buddhism and Korean lifestyle.The colors have many meanings and symbolism, which I have discussed and spoken about in my past post. ⁣⁣

Divination flags 오방기 (Ohbangi) or 길빨 (Ghilpal)  is divination tools used by Daegam 대감 (God of fortune, prosperity and wealth). Flags arent restricted to 대감 only. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Each color also represents a God or Goddess as well. ⁣
°Red represents 산신 (Sanshin)⁣⁣
°Yellow represents 대신 (Daesin)⁣⁣
°White represents 보살 (Bulsa)⁣⁣
°Green represents 동자/동녀 (Donja/Donyeo)⁣⁣
°Blue represents 대감 (Daegam)⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Despite the flags may have their standard meanings like the direction, season and God association. It will still be difficult for laypeople to try and pull flags for guidance and divination on their own. ⁣⁣

description:
⁣Today I'm heading to Williamsburg, Brooklyn. ⁣⁣ ⁣⁣⁣
⁣
FYI, I was pregnant here in this picture ('13)⁣ ⁣
My spirit family and I was called to perform a 고사 (go-sa) ritual to cleanse the land, appease to the local deities, and bring in the winds of abundance, luck and prosperity. Asking the gods to their aid, to bring in good cleansing protective winds. ⁣
For a new business opening to serve the Williamsburg community. ⁣ ⁣
⁣
•What is a GOSA 고사?⁣⁣
It is a blessings ritual, for either a home, new business, construction sites and especially for movie production and premieres. A gosa traditionally can be performed by anyone, setting up an offering table asking the local spirits to bless rather than cause any blockages or mischief. ⁣⁣
Mudangs (shamans) are commission for gosa because nowadays most dont know the proper etiquette to perform such a traditional ritual. Also commissioning  a mudang to perform a gosa is different than a gosa ritual performed by a layperson. The chances of success of a proper gosa in my opinion, is better. ⁣⁣
The mudang has the ability to invoke the gods of her personal pantheon and of the local land. To call the spirits to her through song, dance, music and chants. ⁣⁣
The way we perform the gosa is a small ritual kut in itself, as the Daegam (God of fortune) must be invoked and traced possession by the mudang. Daegam grace and bless us with a promise to help with succession when the offering stands erected on a trident spear over a bowl of sea salt.⁣⁣
Salt acts as a purifying or cleansing agent, to protect and purify the offering to Daegam. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣⁣
-Lately been called to Brooklyn for clients, divination and rituals. Make me kinda wish, I should of never left Bushwick. Maybe one day, I come back to live in Brooklyn. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣

description:
Regularly starting to stir awake at 5am, the first task I set out to do is wash up. I must be clean hygienically before I step into my shrine room for prayers. ⁣Just like I would tidy and clean up my altar daily....I do the same for my body which serves as an altar for my gods.
⁣
Going into prayers, in the darkness of the early morning reminds me of the family matriarch sacrafices. It was OUR mother's and grandmother's who would trek out into the mountains at 3am in straw shoes, to pray to the gods for their protection and blessings.⁣
⁣
Our matriarchs would sacrafice their time, lives and bodies to show their dedication to the gods, through bows of respect and worship. It was the women who had the natural ability to dedicate their life, sacrafice their life to the gods/spirits for the well being of the family. ⁣ ⁣
Prior to converting into Catholicism, my paternal grandmother held many mountain worship rites and rituals alongside with Mudangs. She was tenacious, and a woman of pure strength and unwavering dedication. Although my grandmother wasnt the nicest person to me. I admired GREATLY the dedication, the HOURSSS of daily prayers she did for the betterment of our family. A sacrafice she made that was unnoticed and underappreciated. Growing up whenever grandma went into prayers, we saw it as a nuisance and an embarrassment. Looking at her life now, must of been lonely and what a huge commitment and sacrifices she made for our family. ⁣
Now that it's my turn to uphold my family AND the community, serving as a mudang. My home, life and time is dedicated to my tribe and community. When I rise in the early mornings, I do my bows and prayers like the matriarchs before me....I can finally understand, the struggle, sacrafice and dedication. ⁣
Those straw shoes they wore to trek the mountains, the bows they sacrafice over their bodies.....has become my shoes, my path and 'rock to polish'. ⁣

description:
Mudangs purchase their altar/shrine items from a mudang supply store.  Basic altar items like the water offering bowls, liquor offerings cups, incense holder and altar candle holders are needed when setting up an altar. ⁣ ⁣When the mudang is initiated,  and ready to serve her gods through her own 신당,  2 rituals are performed. First would be the blessing and clearing, it's also a ritual that seeks to harmonize with the local land deity of the home. Its known as a 고사, requiring the traditional offerings within the many parts of the home. Along with a bowl of red bean porridge as it chases and clear any negative spirits. ⁣
The 2nd ceremony/ritual will be the drumming, with the chants/prayers of the mudang. Calling down the gods to be seated within their shrine embodied through murals, folk paintings, calligraphy words, tools associated with the gods, etc. ⁣
When a mudang have to shut her 산당 for whatever reason, no longer serving the gods through a shrine. Then another ceremony/ritual must done to "unseat" the gods, ancestral spirits and deities. It's important to do so, especially after the gods were called down, its proper to send them off. ⁣
What happens to the altar items then? They must be handle with great care and respect, either given back to a mudang store willing to take it. Or take it to a mudang prayer and 굿 camp lodges where they use the items for the many altars. ⁣If the mudang has statues of the gods those cant be discarded improperly, can be given to a Buddhist temple in Korea where they serve them. There has been horror stories of people improperly discarding holy sacred items, with the spirits retaliating.

description:
There are lines even as a mudang 무당, I cant cross. ⁣
⁣
A year or so ago, in a divination....I saw that my stepfather had a dark spot between his chest and stomach. He's  been going to doctors and getting tests done, to find the root cause. ⁣
⁣
Surgery is now schedule in 2 weeks, over half of his stomach needs to be removed. And its quite possibly it has already spread to the liver, but doctors wont say until they open him. They wont confirm what stage he's in, until they open. ⁣
⁣
I knew the winds of samje 잠제 known as the Three Calamities was already starting to shake him. I have experienced and witness how scary 삼재 can be. I tried to convince my mother to have a 병굿 done for him, she declined. ⁣
I spoke to my spirit mother to discuss the possibility of going to perform a Sanshin rite in the mountains. I asked if we set up offerings, drumming and invoking the gods there in the mountains...would it help my step father. I explained my plan was to sit my mother down, discuss and split the cost for this Mountain prayer ritual. ⁣
That's when my spirit mother spoke of my kind heart. She said my kindness could inspire my spirits to help aid. She said all we can do is pray.⁣
I was to told to take a step back, spirit mother said that this is the destiny between them. Whatever it may be. Their choices, their karma, their destiny. ⁣
⁣
⁣
So prayers are up tonight, and every night for him. ⁣

alt_text: Photo by Mudang Jenn 무당젠 on June 24, 2019.

description:
Alot of times we are tested, our beliefs and faith are tested by the gods and deities. They watch carefully how we act and react, constantly throwing obstacles at us to see how we prevail. 
I know, and I can feel what my spirits expectations of me are, as well as mine. It when times are tough, that our faith and beliefs are tested even more. The polishing of one's rock. Just like how the waters will polish a rock smooth, not with brute force but with time, patience and gentleness. Being a shaman isnt about rushing through our journey, its being mindful of the path we walk.
A while ago, I decided to pray, meditate and be in the moment in my shrine room [신당]. My gods and spirits told me that I should not be running and scramble up the mountain, because I might overlook many things. Instead my spirits told me to take one step at a time,  and look around, take in what I see and feel. To enjoy the moment and be aware of the moment, regardless if it's good or bad. My spirits said this is not a race, and not about being in first place. Its about who "dish" is deeper, and holds more water. 
In Korea, we have a saying that not every dish (person) is the same, some are short, shallow, big or deep. My spirits said I must shape my dish slowly, and I must strive to be a dish that's very deep. Deep so that I may hold alot of water, and give back alot of water. [This picture is taken at the mountain top of Ohdaesan, a temple resides. Within these walls, lies the remains of Buddha so it says.]
In times of hardship,  I look to my ancestral spirits, my gods and deities for guidance. description:

My husband tells me I am my own greatest enemy, holding myself to a standard. ⁣
On the gregorian calendar, the full moon is marked for Friday but half way around the world in Korea. Chuseok, the mid autumn festival has already arrived and many are preparing their offering to their ancestors. ⁣
I, being someone who tries to follow the traditions as best I can,  aimed to have my offerings all set up by midnight. ⁣Normally the family gathers to cook and prepare all the offerings. But since I serve the gods, deities and ancestral spirits it part of my duty and service. ⁣

If a mudang doesnt respect her gods with proper etiquette then no one else would. Our communities look to us to lead and guide, trusting in our gods.⁣

description:
Exorcism. ⁣
To cast out negative energy, clearing and cleansing. ⁣
There many ways to perform an exorcism  from sea salt, to burning red pepper flakes, to cooking up - what I call  exorcism stew 찌개. ⁣
⁣
The exorcism ritual was taught directly to me by my elder. The ritual is perform whenever I needed to remove negative energy or casting out any hitchhiking spirit influences.  I usually call upon the gods, goddess and deities to drive out the negative influences. ⁣
⁣
As I was taught, in my chants, one of things we say is "eat and be gone". It refers to any lowly homeless spirits that may be attached. With the exorcism stew, we tell the spirits to eat and leave. When performing this ritual on other people, we take pieces of their hair and other things. We take all this and 'feed' it to the negative forces.⁣
⁣
My 장군칼, spirit tools and weapons of my warlord generals, cuts any attachments and cleans the space. We throw the knives down, and read the way the knives land looking for indicators of a successful exorcism. ⁣ ⁣Picture taken last fall 2018 in Korea at one of the sacred shamanic prayers sites. ⁣

alt_text: Photo by Mudang Jenn 무당젠 on January 20, 2020.

description:
Traditions. What does it mean. ⁣
I have been thinking about the many layered meanings of traditions. ⁣
⁣
For me, traditions means ancestors. Its the story of our ancestors and a way to honor our ancestors. Traditions are woven through the stories of our ancestors. Whenever I practice my traditions, its gives me a deeper understanding of my ancestors, their struggles, hardships and joys. As much beauty is seen in traditions, there is also an equal amount of pain, trauma and suffering. In one way, traditions were born from pain -in some form, a response.⁣
⁣
The traditions of the mudang shaman is to heal, resolve and release of the Korean han, of the people and ancestors. Various kut ceremony were created and performed in response to the situation. To simplify the purpose of mudang, is to bring balance and harmony. It also gives me a sense of pride, especially when much of shamanism was brutally attacked, and survived. ⁣A story of resilience.
⁣
Practicing traditions, means understanding and acknowledging the many stories that are woven in it. I believe honoring ancestors means practicing traditions because its a way, a form of reciting their stories. Keeping our ancestors alive in our every day lives, gives a deeper appreciation. ⁣
⁣
⁣
⁣

description:
A shipment of specially handmade incense just arrived from @zishutraders.⁣
⁣
"Dakpa Tamdin Incense is a traditional Tibetan incense and a Tibetan family owned company based in Nepal.  This incense is pure and hand made, manufactured in accordance with centuries’ old traditional Tibetan formulations and under experienced supervision. The incense recipes were taught to the family by Tertons and Rinpoches who use this incense in their own rituals and on their shrines. It contains traditional Tibetan medicinal herbs and precious substances.  This incense is formulated for religious purposes, meditation, and relaxation." ⁣
⁣
Ribo Sangtsoe means “Mountain Smoke Offering”. This incense can be used to cleanse and purify the mind of impurities, misgivings, stress, and to be filled with spiritual satisfaction and happiness for this life and the next.  Along with prayers and meditation, it is also used while hoisting prayer flags.⁣
⁣
Minling Surpoe (Black) contains ingredients used in the old sacred incense of a Nyingmapa monastery in Tibet alled Mindrolling. It helps create peace of mind in the person using it. This is mainly used for Kyilkhors (Mandalas) as it contains all of the substances and herbs, permitted in Kyilkhors.⁣
⁣
Shingkham Kuenkhyap (Yellow)⁣
Shingkham means “World of the Buddha”, Kuen means “everywhere” and Khyap means “spread.” This incense contains all the requisite herbs and substances required for the rituals to worship and please Gyalwa Rignga’s Shingkham. By offering this incense, we get the blessing of worshipping the Buddhas.⁣
⁣
Sambara (Orange)-⁣
This incense was among the first kinds to be produced in Tibet. It contains all basic herbal ingredients which have been used in Tibet for centuries.  In the Buddhist scriptures, “Dho Tharpa”, it is mentioned that Gyajin (Indra) offered the aroma  Dukpoe to the Buddha himself. From this early document, we learn of the importance of Incense in Buddhism.⁣
⁣
Cant wait to use these special incense in my practice, and give my support to the artist. ✊💗⁣

Sambok refers to the 3 of the hottest days in the 6th &7th lunar month.  Its known as the 3 Dog days, introduced from China during the Qin dynasty. ⁣
Dog days is distinguished by the forecasted negative yin energy and allowing negative spirits to be active. Thus eating red porridge in Dog days helps repel spirits and safeguarding their safety. ⁣

description:
My Janggun regalia spirit armor. ⁣⁣
Janggun 장궁 are military generals, leaders and warlords. ⁣⁣
In Korean shamanism, jangguns are very important gods of the pantheon with their main roles as an exorcist. They are gods of war -fighting, expelling and protecting. In the past national military heroes are deified and some mudangs would serve the historic heroic Jangguns in their shrines. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
One of the modern Janggun some Korean mudangs (shamans) have in their shindang (shrine) is American General Douglas MacArthur. Some Korean mudangs believe Douglas MacArthur spirit has deified, and serve as a janggun spirit and part of their pantheon. ⁣⁣He is a Korean hero who saved Korea during the war, and like every great war hero - his lives on, as a Janggun deity for some mudangs. ⁣⁣
Find it quite interesting and fascinating. Douglas MacArthur and his troops helped defend South Korea when forces invaded from the North during the Korean War. Ever since then, Koreans have viewed America as their savior, and began to idolize America forgetting about America's role towards the annexation and occupation of Korea. ⁣America was in favor of Ito Hirobumi conquest, helped spread propaganda that Korea was unfit to rule our own land. ⁣⁣They allied with Japan and desired our country taken away.
⁣
As a mudang, when researching and learning about my folk traditions and beliefs, its hard to ignore the politics and history that has major factor and impact into shaping our shamanism. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
⁣
*Fun fact: night before my initiation...I dreamt of General Douglas MacArthur as a janggun without knowing about his importance. For those curious, no hes not part of my pantheon. ⁣⁣
⁣

description:
Today being called to my local area for a 고사 GOSA of the home. ⁣
⁣
Our culture and traditions are based on animist views, we believe in spirits of every type. We had tutetary spirits of a home as well known as Gasin 가신. ⁣
⁣
Whenever a home has undergone renovation or any type of construction, its customary that a GOSA blessing ritual is done. ⁣
It's because the very nature of construction is destructive to the environment around us. But also disturbs the local land deities, as well as the tutetary spirits of a home. During construction,  since the spirits dwelling might be disturbed, the gosa will help put back all the spirits and energies back into their rightful place. ⁣
⁣
When erecting a Korean traditional home Hanok, when the roof structure and beams are in place, a GOSA is performed. Because we believe that Korean homes are alive and the house roof beam deity will come and become a tutetary deity that protects the home.⁣
⁣
What are some of the tutetary spirits of the home? ⁣
We have a bathroom deity who is known to despise children, and is enemies with our kitchen deity. So no food in the bathroom. [Maybe this is where my bathroom fear comes from😑] We have door deities, inner quarter deities, pantry deity, and so on. ⁣
⁣
In our traditions, our home is alive and shared with humans and tutetary deities. ⁣ ⁣ ⁣
(Picture of my offerings to my door god, using window ledge as an altar)⁣

My 내림 (Naerim) was a tough a grueling 3 days of exhaustion but I would of not been able to complete such tests without the strength given to me by the gods. Despite that, would I of passed the test of becoming a 무당 in the past? ⁣
⁣
The 내림굿 initiation ceremony would of been much more intense, the shaman-to-be would be put through painstaking tests, that sometimes would claim their lives in the process. The process was intense and hard because it's to test an initiate determination and perseverance, for me it was...ride or die. Silently begging the spirits to heal me, save me from this life, and I was able to transform all my pain, suffering and anguish into tools of compassion, humility and strength.⁣

⁣

description:
⁣
We first open the 굿 invoking the gods, each called down, giving 공수 (channelled divination) to the guests. ⁣
⁣
When 볼살 (Bulsa) grandmother goddess is called, she opens the door to grab one of the ancestral spirit of whom the 굿 is for.⁣
⁣
It's when 대신 (Daesin) Grandmother goddess is invoked that she opens the doors, its through her connection we allow the ancestors spirits to come. ⁣
⁣
Every god/deity is different for every mudang. Two mudangs can have 산신 in their pantheon, but the 산신's will be different. Due to the different ancestors deified to be 산신, and the many different inter positions within a 산신. ⁣
⁣
Not all mudangs have the ability to fully embody, be completely taken over and possessed by an ancestor spirit. It's an innate gift the shaman must be born with, also requiring a very specific 대신 Grandmother Goddess,  since there many types of 대신 roles. ⁣

description:
Tomorrow we have a privately sponsored 칠성제 (Chilseong -je) ritual rites. ⁣
⁣
칠정 (Chilseong) is the God(s) of longevity, especially longevity of children. Known as the 7 stars, and their worships one of the oldest rituals. Comes from the Ursa Major constellation [Big Dipper]. Their 'holiday ' is celebrated on the 7th day of the 7th lunar month. ⁣
⁣
The client, an elderly grandmother wanted a private 칠성 ritual rites for the grandchildren in the family. She wanted to make sure the gods, took extra care of her grandchildren. We prepare long white fabrics with each child information signifying their 'life line'. ⁣Asking the gods like a gardener to care and protect their longevity.
⁣
Year after year, we have multiple 굿 (kut) ceremonies for her family throughout. Despite her frail body, to witness her dedication to the spirits and gods through prayers & bows was truly touching.⁣
⁣
🙏🙇‍♀️⁣
[Picture of a 칠성당 Chilseong shrine on 태백산 Mount Taebak, Korea.] ⁣
See the white cloth of 'life lines' the gods are protecting. ⁣

description:
Great Full Moon (Dae-Boreum) divination. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
The Korean Lunar Full Moon is such an important day of festivals and rituals. Various types of divination is performed by all to predict the upcoming fortune for the year.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
A moon house is built by the community and set on fire. ⁣
•If the Moon House falls or tops over a certain direction, its interpreted to forecast prosperity. ⁣⁣
•If the smoke from the Moon House is so thick and covers the moon, seen as a great omen. ⁣⁣
•The color and the brightness of the Moon is also observed for divination ⁣⁣
•Cows are given special feed mixed rice porridge with different beans. If the cow eats the rice first, then it forecast great rice agriculture, if beans are eaten other crops will flourish. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
These are just some of the divination types that were used by the Korean people and ancestors. The first Lunar Full Moon is such an important evil chasing ritual festival that sets the tone for the upcoming year, helps people prepare. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⁣
What it means - we were always in contact and in communication with the natural world. We give offerings, cleansing and raise the 'spirits energy'. Achieving balance with the spiritual and the humanly. ⁣

description:
How do you define a calling? Why is that ppl question my path/judgement, is it because its not the norm. Would you question a person who felt the calling to submit their life to God by becoming a priest? Or question someone who wants to shave their head, and become a Buddhist monk? 
The process of becoming a priest is institutionalized. Going to theology priest school, obtaining a degree and finally getting their certification, passing their exam...like a lawyer or doctor. That process does not certify their ability to become a priest, validate their spiritual calling or guarantee their life path be straight.
Someone asked me if I was certified. I didnt know whether to laugh or get angry. Like as if an institution can verify if I am a shaman mudang or not, sounds ridiculous to me. Its not a list of credits I need, or series of written test I need to pass. 
Shamanism existed long before ANY religion ever came to. Its found all over the world practiced by the earliest civilizations. Its not an imported belief like Christianity or Catholicism. Pls dont think I am attacking other beliefs, just asking for open mindedness.

Its also winter solstice,  and traditionally in my korean culture we eat 'ppat juk' which is red bean porridge. Usually people will gather in their homes to perform ancestral rites before eating their porridge, and they also put out a bowl of porridge put into every room to ward off the negative spirits. Nowdays this practice is not done by today's Koreans. 
But I am ironically very traditional despite my upbringing. I will provide red bean porridge as my offerings, and perform a cleansing rite and putting porridge in every room of my house to cleanse and purify. Have an amazing winter solstice and a beautiful full moon everyone.

description:
巫 is the character for "shaman", in the Chinese "WU" and Korean "MU". This character has undergone many changes with time but its said to date back 1 B.C. or even further back. Some of the earlier characters represents two jade pieces crossing each other, or two bones piece crossing. Another version of the earlier character is a pictogram [2nd pic] that depicts a woman with "long sleeves". It literally depicts a woman dancing so good that she wields extraordinary mystical power using her hands. She dances so beautifully that even that she can invite the gods from the Heavens. 
A character so simple looking with deep meaning, and I was so elated that it literally meant a kut [굿] ritual ceremony. In our kut rituals we call down and invoke our gods, to sing and dance. We [the mudangs] channel our deities, entertaining them. We invoke our gods so they can help, aid the clients with a wish fulfilled. 
The 巫 character had many meanings like witch, witchcraft, sorcerer and shaman. [Not to say, witches nowadays are shamans, although there are similarities and parallels but there are differences. Shamans in the Korean mudang traditions requires an initiation ceremony naerimkut [내림굿] which requires the invocation of the gods and sitting them.]

description:
There is a saying amongst Korean mudang shaman (무당) and Buddhist monks (스님) that when a child had their umbilical cord wrapped around his/her neck. Their fate destiny saju (사주) is to become either a 무당 (mudang) and/or 스님 (monk). When my spirit mom was born, with her umbilical cord around her neck. A high level monk asked her mom to give away the baby so that she can train to become a high level monk at a temple in the mountain. 
The umbilical cord wrapped around the neck is a sign of predestined fate to walk a path of higher consciousness, and serve the gods/deities. 
My spirit mom said made sense since I am a mudang shaman, and this baby being gifted from the gods. That this child shall walk a similar path to mine. description:
My daily ritual for my sindang (신당), my temple, altar and sacred space. 
Most are curious about my daily life, my daily rituals for my altar and sacred space. 
I try to do most of my daily rituals in the morning, but sometimes its difficult with 2 rambunctious boys, 3 boys (if you include my hubs). Before walking into temple, its seen as proper to wash up and enter the sacred space with a clean body. A sacred space must be entered with pure mind, heart and body, this is where my spirits, my gods and ancestors are venerated, so I want to be always mindful. 
I empty my water offering bowls, and fetch new clean water from the sink. I have a water pot specifically for my temple only, its purpose is for water offerings only. I do not mix any of my personal items with the items of the spirits, including bowls, plates or whatever I use in my temple. 
Candles are lit, and water offerings is given to the middle first, the left second, the right third and to my house guardian out in my foyer lastly. Next up is my liquor offerings done in the same respect and manner. 
Last part is when I light an incense,  which I light from the candle. I never ever blow out the flame that lit the incense, and instead I shake it gently between two hands to snuff out the flame. Everything must be done in a mindful manner. The offerings we give is important, but its even more important - to be mindful of the offerings we give to the gods, of our hearts and mind when performing these daily ritual. Fetching water and pouring the water offerings is not what this lesson is about....anyone can fetch and pour water. Its about the openness, the depth of our gratitude in our hearts and mind, while we pour the water and other offerings.

What is a Mudang ?
The word "mu" is ancient word describing a shaman-priest intermediary between the first god, gods of nature and humans in the korean indigenous religion. 
The men shaman priest are usually called bak-su, and mudangs are referred to women. The baksu word is an adaptation of Siberian names for male shamans baksi, balsi, bahsih, etc. 
Mudang is a priestess who employs magic to effect cures, tell fortune, soothe the spirits of the dead, repulse evils, and so forth. Mudang (mostly) has hereditary abilities to contact the spirit world, inhabited by various shamanic gods and deities. 
No person chooses the path of a mudang voluntarily, even if its hereditary. The path of a mudang involves alot of grief and loneliness, misunderstanding and ridicule. Only the true mudangs are chosen by the spirits experiencing sinbyeong known as the divine sickness, shamanic sickness, spirit sickness, etc.

We made our way to the next destination,  to the underwater tomb of the Great Munmu Daewang. Our beloved Dragon King of the sea. 
We rented a table alongside the beach, that would give us shelter from the winds. There, other mudangs were scattered across the beach, all drumming and praying with their offerings. 
Even Buddhist monks were there with their own clients, hitting their moktaks. Praying to the Dragon King in a ceremony/ritual where they purchase back a fish, and release it into the waters. 
Amazing sight it was to see monks and mudangs side by side. Other monks rented rooms that looks like a small 신당 "sindang'. Through the window, I can see that he was jumping up and down, while banging on his cymbals. At first I was extremely fascinated, and then I became upset. The Buddhist has their culture, their traditions and ways rooted from India. But why is it that these monks, steal from the Mudangs? Our ceremonies, dance and songs through imitation? 
Ive had plenty of clients who came to me for readings, wanted to find out the reason and source for their unhappiness and life misfortunes. When they walk into my "sindang" 신당, I see their spirits and ancestors. I tell the clients that they have to send away the spirits that pesters them. Most of them tell me that they did such ceremonies with the monks at temples. This is dangerous, because their methods has no effect on the godly world of spirits, ancestors and gods. Why is it so many are against Mudangs? We are demonized but then everyone imitates us? We live in a world full of patriarchal dominance, and Mudangs are [mostly] females holding the power, that must be scary to the men.

description:
What's the shamanic aspect of mental illness like bipolar disorder, or multiple personality and schizophrenia. What's the shamanic aspect of hiccups? 
I constantly get messages about people asking me about my perspective on their mental illness and instability. I am NOT a doctor, I cannot replace what doctors, therapy and other treatments can do for mental illness. 
Yes, sometimes there can be a reason why a person's mental state can be spiritual influenced but that does not mean its every case. Please seek out medical attention. With spiritual arts exploding in popularity with reiki, witches, shamans and other spiritual paths, there are many articles how mental illness is treated by spiritual leaders. I cannot say how dangerous that is as a shaman myself. It's best to go seek a doctor, especially in cases when people are severely ill. 
Yes, in some cases working with a shaman can help but that isnt every case. Just like taking vitamin supplements helps a person immune system or help with their calcium,  it does not replace doctors. 
Working with the gods, deities and spirits means to work in conjunction,  working together while receiving aid/treatment from doctors medically. 
I've seen and witnessed firsthand how powerful my shamanic lineage can be with  successful outcomes of a kut 굿 ceremony/ritual but I would never ever advise anyone to dismiss their doctors. 
Please if you suspect anyone is suffering,  do not it go untreated. Please find a proper doctor with merit, and seek professional advice and diagnosis.
Working together in conjunction I believes provides the best outcome helping fill in the gaps. 
NO shaman can help cure your dental issue, if your teeth is rotting away. No amount of drumming and ritual ceremony can help restore your tooth, or your heart. It doesnt work in that sense. So please seek out medical treatment.

description:
(Part 2/2)
My culture we had a social class system, the noble ruling class of aristocrats Yangban. The lowest  is the Cheonmin, and it was mainly due the professions that were seen as 'unclean' like butchers, metalworkers, the shoemakers, kiaseng and mudangs, etc. 
A mudang will train a entire lifetime, and when one fails at being a shaman....we became kiaseng,  entertainers of the ruling yangban class. A mudang is an entertainer of the gods, the spirits. To be an initiated mudang, or marked by the spirits does not guarantee immediate success. One must know how to dance gracefully, seamlessly in between the thin veil between the living and the spirits. 
Spirit mother shook her head in disbelief how the many mudang [shamans] act like they are above others, showing off lavish lifestyles and prancing about. She looked at me, and told me to never forget why we became a mudang, why we are chosen. 
A mudang means a lifetime of service, lifetime of struggles, of many sufferings and hardships. Why? Why is that? 
Its to repent, its karma, to make up for the many lifetimes of sin, and bad karma we committed collectively. That process of 'polishing our rock', she told me to polish, and polish, and polish....a lifetime of polishing for our ancestors, our karma and our future children. The more we 'polish' the more our gods, our spirits,  our ancestors can rise from the chains of their own karma. This is why we are working a lifetime of service, of prayers for ourselves and our seekers. We carry the karma and the weight of our clients, we build up ourselves so we can serve the gods and mankind. 
This is truly a heavy weight to carry, when a mudang commits a sin...it is a strike against our gods and ancestors, and ourselves. When we commit harmful acts, we prevent the path of our spirits...and therefore preventing our own, cutting off our own lifeline. 
This is a deep lesson that always stays with me, and constantly echos. When my time comes to meet my gods in the spirit world, I truly hope I can stand tall with honor and integrity.

description:
Sotdae 솟대. 
Birds are seen as messengers of the spirits in the Korean shamanistic traditions. Its is assumed that the sotdae is deprived from connection of the 'Cosmic Tree' and 'Sky Birds'. Sotdae are spirit poles like totem but different. Long poles out of either wood or stone, with a bird figure on top. The significance of the poles is prevalent in North Asian shamanism and related to the world-axis whic connects the heavens to the earth. 
The bird figures were never carved, instead kept original wood shape, only de-barked to show natural beauty. Many bird types of sotdae were found like geese, magpie or crows but ducks were mostly used. Ducks were given important meanings due their ability on land, water, and air was thought they they can control rain, survive floods and protect villages from fires. Ducks were also part of Koreas founding myth.
Originally placed at the village entrance along with the Jangseun (totem) to wish for peace and good harvest. 
During the Joseon period, sotdae symbolized when a scholar passed a government entrance exam for celebration. A sotdae facing South to wish for good weather for farming,  facing North meant to bring rain.

description:
Jowangsin [조왕신] the goddess of the kitchen hearth and fire. This shamanic deity has long been revered by housewives since the early 3rd century.Jowangsin is a gasin, a branch of deities that protects the home.  The goddess is personified into an offering bowl of water perched on an altar above the hearth. Offerings of fresh new water must be given daily, with a prayer. On special occasion, rice cakes, fruits, with rice and other offerings are set on a table for the deity. The kitchen served as a symbol of good fortune, a good fire indicated wealth. The goddess also serves a role as a scribe, writing down and recording all the daily happenings of the home and family, reporting it to the Heavens. 
Jowangsin deity has 5 rules one must follow when in her kitchen perimeter. (1) No cursing (2) Do not put your feet up on her hearth (3) Dont sit on her hearth (4) Maintain a clean kitchen (5) You may worship other kitchen deities. 
Due to the status of Jowangsin as gasin, she is a lowly deity compared to the Heavenly deities like Chilseong or Sansin. She is not a deity that is presented in an illustrated form like the other gods, though her role is important within the household. 
Jowangsin is most indefinitely a goddess, but the few images available online interestingly, depicts a male. The kitchen god, is also a deity that is widely worshipped in China, and is portrayed as a male. Some korean Buddhist temples have an altar with an male image of Jowangsin. Alot of shamanic deities, roots and myths have been rewritten to serve the Buddhist views. In my opinion, there are misgnonism aspects of Buddhism being a patriarchal system side weeping the matriarchs of Korean shamans.
I dont have a personal altar for Jowangsin within my home, but on many important holidays I do set up grand offerings in my kitchen, paying my respects to Jowangsin.

description:
Those who are chosen/marked by the spirits assume that once initiated as a mudang, your sufferings ends. I answer that yes/no. 
Yes the suffering you endured (shinbyeong, shaman sickness, spirit sickness) or whatever other names its called, that stops. The ancestral sickness you had because of your ancestors spirits at your side, that too, stops.
I geniunely feel for those who are suffering, living a life that feels like a curse, those who cant make sense of what is and isnt, etc. But because of our sufferings, it is what gives us the ability to connect with those whose soul may be suffering silently. 
I had it hard. In school I use to get bullied, I was shy, quiet and weird. Weird because I use to talk about demons, ghosts and spirits. Hated school bathrooms. Hated dark hallways. Went to alot psychics only to be told it was a family curse. Dreams started to become vivid, almost screaming at me. Sleep paralysis episodes was so frequent it made me terrified of the night. Visions happen impairing me briefly for that moment, I was scared shit.
But despite all that and more, I grew from it. I learned compassion and empathy at a young age. It doesn't matter if your saju says you are mudang shaman, or that you are talented/gifted all the fields of our work. You got to put the effort, polish your rock, walk in a path that aligns with your soul and spirits. 
Suffering is the magical main ingredient to what makes a great mudang shaman. Its beautifully bittersweet. We are also misunderstood, but it comes with the path.

description:
This is my most precious set of hanbok (한복), this was worn on my last day of initiation (3rd day). The day I "married" my spirits and received my heavenly mandate
An initiate must always have 2 (two) sets of new hanbok for their initiation. One is worn during the first two intense days of initiation, and last clean new set is worn when the mudang receive their mandate. 
One set has a yellow top/red dress bottom, and the other has a green top, red dress bottom. The colors of the hanbok is crucial and hold lots of meaning. Yellow jeogori top 저고리 with red chima bottom 치마 are the colors of unmarried girls. Green jeogori top with a red chima bottom are the colors of marriage. We (mudangs) are getting "married" to our gods 신, when we get intiated. That's why I wore this set on last day of initiation, it's my wedding hanbok of sorts. It's the core basics, etiquette and respect. The foundations which we lay on is important! 
White is color of death, mourning and underwear. I have seen initiates wear color white hanbok on their initiation day. It's like saying your initiation is your death, you went to meet your gods in sheer undergarments or you are in mourning, in our traditions. Usually after that, we are free to wear other types and styles of hanbok when working in a ceremony. 
How many sets should I get made.

Had a client today, it was an elderly man with a hearing problem. 
Helped him into my shrine room, and he came with a stack of papers. He sat down and told me he was so fustrated, he didn't have a person to speak with so, he came to me to find some peace.  Born in 1937, when Korea was still under Japanese occupation. He said most of his life, for his meals all he grew up with was a side of [gochujang] and cabbage kimchi. White rice was a precious grain, and it was a seasonal food they rarely had on their table. 
He also told me that he entered school in the first grade at 10 yrs old. In school, there were many ranges of kids from 8 to 16 years old, attending the first grade. Mostly education was invested in boys, as the girls stayed home and learned how to run the household and kitchens. 
While serving the military , his father passed away in an accident. Although the family was poor, they had a few parcels of land. He was so busy with working and providing for his family,  that he never thought about the land until many, many years later. He was able to sell one land piece for 2 sacks of rice, and other land he had no idea what happened. 
He told me that he went to Korea 2 years ago to visit the burial of his parents, he was heartbroken that their gravesite wasnt managed or maintained, it pained him dearly. 
He was furious at his uncles, because he suspected it was them who deceived his mother and sold off his fathers land without seeing a nickel from it. He was upset, sad and filled with han. He humbly put his hands together and bowed before my gods enshrined in my thankka. He asked for the answers, I relayed the messages from my spirits and he sat still and listened. His back was curved, shoulders drooped and hung his head low as I felt his injustice.

description:
Peach Blossoms. 🍑
Peaches are usually a sign, a symbol for the spring season. Most people think of the peach, as a sign of good luck, fortune and longevity. 
But the peach [the fruit and the tree] has another role within the Korean shaman customs. It is use to drive out spirits, ghosts, negativity and exorcism. Since peach represents spring of the yang [energy], it is most effective tool against warding off negative spirits. 
This is why peaches are NEVER ever put on the offering tables for the ancestors [jesa] and for the gods/deities. 
Peaches are also in fact, a fruit that is depicted within murals and paintings of the gods/deities. The fruit of the spirits, represents good luck and fortune, but the fruit shown in the paintings are not the same "type". These are the heavenly peaches growing within the heavenly realms of the gods and deities, so it's not same "peach" as the one grown on this earthly plane. 
The peach has a long history within the shamanic rituals of the mudangs, that it is even revered in the shaman songs called muga. 
So when setting up any offering table to ancestors or spirits, please be mindful not to put any peaches or other stone fruits like plums, nectarines, apricots, cherries, etc.

description:
(Part 1 of 2)
Most people are curious who I am, how did I end up on my path. Questions about me, as a human and as a person. So for those to get to know a little more about me. 
Born and raised in NYC, lived all my life here. Both parents immigrated from Seoul, Korea in the early 80s. I'm the eldest of three. 
I did not come from a complete family, in fact my early childhood and home life is quite dysfunctional and broken. My parents divorced at the age of 9, and my mother walked out of our lives due to the intense abusive situation with my father. He was an alcoholic and a domestic abuser. We moved from place to place, under the care of my grandmother and our aunts from my father side. He worked hard all day and night running a 24 hour small grocery store to provide for the family. 
Growing up was certainly not easy due to the abusive nature of all my family.  My cousin who was in charge of us, gave us corporal punishment of holding chairs above our heads for hours while on our knees. Sometimes she would make us plank while beating down on our backs with rods and sticks. She had a lot of trauma of her own, but the adults in our life left her unchecked. Aware of the abuse but turned the other cheek. 
My family was strict Catholic,  an intense type of Catholic that is not normally followed by the Church.  My grandmother held her own rosary prayers at night, and station of the cross which I was forced to attend and endure. Every weekend we drive to LI, and pray at the outdoor shrine of the "Shrine of our Lady". We always went at midnight, despite weather conditions. Rain and snow did not stop us, just meant we had to layer more. I use to look at the stars in the sky and wonder if heaven knew my pain. 
I went from a bright bubbly child to a shy, timid person afraid to speak and show my personality. School was the worse, I went to a Catholic school called Queen of Peace. Which didn't help me either due to the severe bullying and teacher picking on me.

description:
Happy Lunar New Year aka Korean New Year. 
We call this day 설날 Seollal. 
The first day of the Korean lunar calendar. It is one of the most significant holiday, celebration lasting 3 days.
Earliest record of this celebration was in the 3rd century. 
Its an important day to return to your hometown, prepare an offering table to past ancestors. The ancestor offering ritual is called charye or jesa. 
When family visits their elders, we perform Sebae 세배. Its worshipping of your family elder, a ritual act of respect and filal piety. Sebae involve the act of bowing to pay our respect to the elders. Usually you perform one bow to your living elders and three bows to deceased ancestors. 
Children would receive money from the elders, and carry them in silk pouches while dressed in traditional korean clothing called hanbok. 
Along with the traditional offerings of fruit, rice cake, liquor, water, vegetable, tofu, fish, meat. Its a special day to eat rice cake soup called tteukgook. Its made of white rice cake signifying purity and cleanliness. 
My children gods ask me for money, so I put some under their shoe in their altar and then put it in their silk pouches. 
Happy New Year 🤗

description:
Chilseong [칠성], the "Seven Star" shamanic deity of the Big Dipper constellation. It is said, in the Korean night sky, the big dipper constellation stars shined the brightest. The chilseong worship is one of the oldest within the shamanic culture, revered by woman for their family households and by mudang [shamans]. [Chilseong] is thought to be the protector of the Korean people.  Governing the lifeline longevity of the people, health, peace and most importantly, the health and life span of children. Until a child is 7 years old, their health and life line is under the care of Samsin, but afterwards, it is looked after by Chilseong under their care.
Chilseong is a Heavenly deity, usually depicted as 7 men but idolized as one shamanic deity. Among the 7 stars, there is usually a leader, the one who holds the book of consciousness. 
At the time of Buddhist introduction, the two most prominent shamanic god/deities were Sanshin [god of mountain/earth] and Chilseong. It was important for Buddhism to absorb these two shamanic deities, as they help give rise to the Buddhist and Taoist movement. 
Spirit mom told me monks were first wandering peddlers that people ignored, their beliefs and teachings wasnt accepted. It was the mudangs who helped clothe and feed the starving monks. They in return used our gods for their advantage.
Every year there is a day dedicated to Chilseong,  offerings tables are set and the names of children are written on long white cloth to ask for their blessings and protection. This year I will have both my boys participate in the ritual to have the names written in the stars, asking for Chilseong' grace

description:
@merlegeode ask me share my story behind my logo. Ask what is my story, and how I came to choose this. 
The 5 colors of red, blue, white, yellow and green represents the colors on the Korean shaman culture. Each colors has various meanings, representing the 5 directions, seasons, and also indication of the gods and deities. These same colors are deeply rooted in the culture, on clothing, food and architecture influencing the Korean lifestyle. 
I chosed to have it be represented in the form of the Rose of Sharon, the national flower of Korea known as 무궁화 [Mugunghwa] a flower that symbolized the independence of Korea. Mugung means everlasting or immortal, and hwa meaning flower. The five petals also represents the 5 traditional types of happiness, duty unity all translating to the peace and happiness. There's even a song we sing dedicated to the flower "Mugunghwa, Mugunghwa our flower of the nation/ land". The Sam-Taeguk (tricolor)symbol of the red, yellow and blue used in Korean shamanism represents Cheon-Ji-In, which means Heaven, Earth and Humanity going back to the Joseon period. Widely used everywhere in the Korean culture. 
I wanted the symbols with deep historical meanings to come together in the form of a simple mandala. Bringing me back to the beginnings of my spiritual journey, where I would sit under trees meditating and drawing mandalas. 
In a way, my logo, my personal symbol tells the story of my path, my growth. And it all came to me in a vision. 
Thank you for allowing me to share, and many thanks to Merle, for suggesting this. Please ask me, anything you would like for me to share/discuss as I'm bursting with stories to tell. 😁

My aunt told me that when they lived in the countryside of Korea, down the dirt road a new church was being built.  Most of the villagers did not pay much attention or care for this Catholic faith. To entice the locals the Church started to offer meals and even promote money loans. It was not so long after the Korean war, and everyone was trying to rebuild their lives. When the Church offered money to the locals, that is when everyone lined up and eventually got baptized due to the monetary incentive. 
Before then my grandmother was a follower of the musok/mugyo traditions. 
Due to the acceptance of a new faith and path, my grandmother was never able to fulfill her role and path as a mudang. 
During my the last offerings of the new moon, as I went into my prayers I saw a quick glimpse, or a 'vision' of my grandmother standing outside of my home. It was for a few seconds, and I ignored it because I doubted myself. Soon afterwards I would see red eyes everywhere but I did not connect the two things together. It wasn't until the ceremony we had last Friday, when the clients ancestors spirit invoked and possessed by my spirit mother is when the messages were passed over to me. 
The ancestor said the spirit of my grandmother follows me, and when this disciple [me] cries it isn't me who is crying but the influence of my grandmother's spirit. She [my grandmother] is crying and cant move on into the spirit world because of her excessive 'han'. The ancestor warned if I dont perform a ceremony/ritual to help her pass, and if shaking me alone is not enough then she will start shaking my children. 
The message I heard, stayed with me, and I was ready to set a date for my ancestors kut ceremony that night. That is when I remembered my oldest son, started having nightmares every day for the last week or two,  he tells me someone chases him and he sees red eyes. Immediately I knew that the 'red eyes' he was referring to was the same eyes I seen.

description:
Temple care is essential and crucial to korean shamans known as mudang/manshin/bosal.

In the beginning I used to just pour the water, just to pour as a sign of respect. But over time I learned that when I pour water into their bowls, it's not just pouring them water. It is the intentions that I have, the Gratitude and gratefulness that I have when I give my offerings.
A lot of my students tend to look beyond the horizons not realizing the crucial building blocks they are missing to develop the relationship with their spirit, gods and ancestors. Relationships are not born overnight and it applies to a shaman. After being initiated.... there is no way, you are able to differentiate between your gods and spirit. It feels like a giant ball of Play-Doh mixed in with colors, and as you develop your relationships you will begin to understand and differentiate.
The spirits chooses the shamans, but that does not mean our destiny comes to us with no sweat, tears or work involved.

description:
"Hi, my name is XYZ and I want to learn more about my ancestral indigenous beliefs and traditions."
I get the same messages everyday. 
I am so happy that many Korean diaspora are searching for their roots. 
It gives me hope that the younger generation is more open minded and becomes more aware, conscious and mindful. "Dear XYZ, Thank you so much for contacting me. My name is 신수보살 (Sinsu Bodhisattva) fully practicing in NY....."
The best way to learn about Mugyo is to establish a relationship with a practicing and properly initiated mudang/manshin/bosal. First step is to get a reading, then go from there. Ask about any holidays, or special rite you can do from home with their guidance and supervision. 
Most get upset that there isn't much one can do on their own with the spirits like other spiritual paths. Someone asked me if there was a "Korean" way of doing a love spell found on a pagan/witchcraft site. Or if there is a way to incorporate Hellenistic or Kemetic gods/deities with our indigenous gods/deities. 
Like what?...
Who would ever..
Sigh. 
Guys, there is a reason why I say to establish a relationship with a properly trained and initiated mudang shaman. This isn't some thing you can wave your smudge stick and meditate away. It's a reason why people are chosen are marked by the spirits, why they are called and not you. If you are interested in learning more about Mugyo, or any spiritual paths of other indigenous traditions do it under the proper guidance.
I will happily and seriously spend my time helping anyone with their questions about this path or their life. You don't have to be Korean to get a reading to glimpse and see our ways, our views and reasonings. 
Love you IG tribe, the open hearted, the mindful.

description:
Part (1/4)  Alot of people have 신기 (energy of spirits) or influenced by them in one way or another. There are alot of different spirit sickness types in our traditions but it still takes a special person to become a mudang. 
Once a person is initiated, you are a newborn, and you will need to be guided. I dont care what the person's Saju says NO one is born amazing. The road we walk isnt smooth, its filled with jagged edges, obstacles, and many elements that try to influence us to falter from our truth. 
Some people want to become initiated because it fills their ego, they think that they will become an 'all powerful being' with the spirits at their fingertips. 🤬 Jafar from Aladdin didnt realize the great deal of service it means, and later chained and imprisoned. 
Those who abuse their power and spirits will later become chained and imprisoned, not knowing it. Created their own demise, and the sin they commit becomes a strike against your spirits/gods tainting their light. I too made many mistakes, and learn from those gravely because they come back to you over and over. 
It was March, just a mere 6 months passed after my initiation in Korea. I was a newborn, didnt know much. One day someone reached out for a reading, one of my first online reading. Took us 3 hours, with lots of tears, crying and stories. We connected and then 1 month later, her entire family flew over to me. For a week and half, we prayed in the mountains and the oceans, and then we initiated her for 3 long hard days. 
She was older than me, could of been my mother. Her health was on a decline, with heart isssues and lungs that burned, we worried how will she get through 3 days of initiation. The first day of kut, she flew....
We were amazed how someone so sick could manage such hard strenuous jumps. As she jumped, tears filled my eyes because I knew the reason. The same bittersweet pain was staked in my heart, not a dry eye in the temple. Everyone gathered to support our new sister, but we all cried sharing her pain, we all mourned together.

description:
In the sacred shamanic mountains of Ilwolsan, named after the 'Sun-moon' connection and its deep sacred shamanic roots. This mountain is also known for its haunted peak, roamed by a particular ghost or spirit. 
In one of the shrines, prayer temples we visited is a small wooden structure dedicated to Hawng-ssi-buin 황씨 부인 [means Mr. Hwangs wife]. The legend goes to say, that Mrs. Hwang ran away from the terrible abuse of her mother in law, and ended up committing suicide deep in the valley of this mountain. Due to her 'han' 한 [trauma, anger and/or injustice] her spirit was not at rest, and she would haunt this mountain. Some say that she brings misfortune to those disloyal,  greedy and abusive,  while she bestows blessings on those are kind, generous and good hearted. 
The story the shrine keeper told me goes a bit deeper. It was said due to her 'han' of injustice and pain, she would appear to the local villagers. Until her husband who felt so sorry for her and remorseful for what happened, enshrined her giving her offerings  and performing ceremony/ritual to help appease the spirit. (I dont know how true the next part is.....BUT)
It is said since then, that is when shamans [mudangs] started to incorporate and 'grab the ancestors' so that they may 'untie' the knots to release ancestrals 'han' and fury. ☀️🌙 I should add, that not every mudang can grab the ancestors,  its different than seeing or sensing an ancestor. To have the ability to 'grab' the ancestors spirit successfully...one must be born with the innate gift, and you also need a specific god deity for that task. Without theose two, it is seen as other mudang try and fumble around with the 'grabbing ancestors' part of the kut ceremony.

description:
Happy full moon, the Great Moon festival. 
It's known as 대보름 [Dae Bo-reum], the festival of the 'Great Full Moon' and the 1st full moon of the new Lunar Year. 
It's an auspicious day, and traditionally sacrifices were made to the Heavens in offerings, or lighting of the lanterns. 
There are so many traditions in respect to this full moon. Some traditions are cracking walnuts with teeth, or climbing the mountain to witness the 1st sun rise, or stealing mud from wealthy homes, etc. 
The main custom is to eat 오곡밤 [O-go-bap] which is rice mixed with other grains and various beans, along with side dishes of only vegetables namuls and nuts. This customary meal helped people replenish nutrients that was lost during the cold winter months when food was scarce. 
There are many celebrated folk traditions and customs associated with this day. One the folk games villagers and children would play was the game of tug-of- war. 
Mask dances served as exorcism to expel evil and bring good fortune to the villagers. 
I wish everyone a very prosperous Lunar Year. I hope everyone had a great first Lunar full moon.

description:
Todays kut ceremony/ritual is a 재수굿 [jesu kut], a ritual to bring in more luck, blessings and prosperity abundance. The clients are Russian, operating a construction business in Brooklyn. 
Their 1st ceremony was last year, a sickness ceremony for their young daughter who has a medical condition of constantly falling asleep. 
Today, they asked that the gods bless their business and family fortune. The wife and her son, were both entering their samje and we used specialized tailsman and effergy dolls. 
Because it is a jesu kut, we will be using a whole pig offering to Daegam [대감]. When raising of the pig, if it stands quickly it means that things will work out quickly. If the pig sway back and forth a bit and then stand, means it will take some time to find stability but in the end, things will work out. Based on how the pig stands, foretells us by the Daegam deityhow soon or quickly,  luck will find them. 
Daegam is the god deity that most pray to for business,  prosperity and wealth. He is the state official that oversees family fortune and wealth. Most businesses, would have a small shrine [danji] with offering bowls to Daegam to bring in prosperity. 
We pray, we ask the gods to hear the pleas of our hearts as we work diligently, with our lives on the line to bring in the prosperity.

description:
•Do you see the crow perched on top of the tree? 🐦
Birds are seen as messengers of the gods, between heaven and earth and many birds are considered sacred like the magpie, ducks, cranes and etc. 
On my way up the difficult trail of Manisan 마니산, I reached a point when I seriously contemplated if I should continue climbing up to its summit or if I should call it quits. my legs trembled as it carry me up the mountain side. 
While sitting and feeling defeated a crow just happen to be above my head in a tree. It squawked as if it called to me, to get my attention. I thought to myself if it was the spirits (as a joke) but just then it started to laugh at me. 'ka-ka-ka-ka' as if taunting me on my defeat. 
Did not think anything of it, until the bird flew to my right side and perched on the handrail. It cawed and squawk again but the sound was different. 'Hana-dul, hana-dul, hana-dul' it screamed. 
At that very moment I wanted to collapse from emotions because my grandfather used to say that. He would say 'hana deul, hana dul' as he always walked because his legs didn't work well. "Hana" is korean for number 1. "Dul" is the Korean number for 2. 
the crow flew in front of me still cawing 'Hana-dul, hana-dul. 
Took a picture to remember this moment.  I picked myself up. 'hana-dul, hana dul'
I counted as I silently cried my way up to its peak.

description:
(Photo from Google)
Today is new moon offerings. Yesterday was Columbus day or Indigenous People's Day.
Honoring our ancestors and natural spirits was a normal way of life. The man in the picture has set an offering table to the local town guardian. These town guardian known as jangseung (장슨) are wooden totem poles of Korea. Located at the entrance of the village,  to ward off evil and protect the villagers within. Jangseung were worshipped as gods, often the town held ceremonial rites to give thanks to the guardian deity. 
Jangseung, the Korean totem pole has also been found on roads to provide companionship and protection to the travellers. They are made to resemble the villagers, a symbol of their ability to stand tall despite many difficulties. 
Happy belated Indigenous Day. 
Happy 초하루, new moon.
